bull.b: The strong revenue rebound and higher gross margin show meaningful improvement in commercial performance and product economics. If retained, this progress can expand the operating base, support better absorption of costs, and provide a foundation for more durable profitability over the next several quarters.

A shift from heavy prior cash burn to positive operating and free cash flow is an important quality improvement. Although the cushion is currently small, internally generated cash can reduce financing dependence and support operations if the recent revenue recovery remains in place.

The reported increase in assets, cash, and shareholders’ equity indicates that the company entered the latest period with somewhat stronger financial resources. This improvement can support working-capital needs and strategic execution, even though leverage remains a material constraint.

bear.b: Debt remains slightly above equity and the reported leverage ratio is still elevated despite improvement from 2025. This structure can restrict investment flexibility, increase sensitivity to operating setbacks, and leave less financial capacity to fund growth or absorb cyclical weakness.

bear.t: Persistent net losses and volatile profitability
bear.b: The company remains loss-making after all costs, while EBITDA is only modestly positive and historical results have been volatile. That pattern weakens confidence that the recent recovery is durable and leaves earnings vulnerable if revenue growth or gross-margin improvement moderates.

bear.t: Free cash flow lacks a durable cushion
bear.b: Although cash generation has recently turned positive, free cash flow is only marginally above zero and has worsened sharply from the prior annual period. Limited cash coverage reduces resilience if margins soften or working capital reverses, potentially increasing reliance on external financing.
